title: Reporting statements (2): verb tenses in that-clauses
summary: Согласование времён в придаточных косвенной речи: сдвиг **backshift**, неизменяемые формы, случаи, когда сдвиг не нужен.
ru:
## Основное правило: сдвиг времён (backshift)
Если вводный глагол стоит в прошедшем времени (**said, told, explained, thought**), то глагол в придаточном обычно «отодвигается» на один шаг назад:
- present simple → **past simple**: > "I work here." → She said she **worked** there.
- present continuous → **past continuous**: > "I'm leaving." → He said he **was leaving**.
- present perfect → **past perfect**: > "We've signed it." → They said they **had signed** it.
- past simple → **past perfect** (или остаётся past simple): > "I lost the key." → She said she **had lost** the key.
- past continuous → **past perfect continuous** (или остаётся): > "It was raining." → He said it **had been raining**.
- **will → would**, **can → could**, **may → might**, **shall → should**, **is going to → was going to**, **must → had to**.
Это не «механическое» правило: цель — показать, что слова были сказаны в прошлом.

## Что не меняется
- **would, could, should, might, ought to, used to, had better, needn't, mustn't**: > "You should rest." → She said I **should** rest.
- **past perfect** остаётся: *"I had already left."* → *He said he **had** already left.*
- **Условные и гипотетические формы**: > "If I were you, I'd apply." → She said that if she **were** me, she'd apply.
- **must** для вывода (предположение): > "She must be tired." → I thought she **must be** tired.

## Когда сдвиг не обязателен
Сдвиг не нужен, если:
1. вводный глагол в настоящем времени или present perfect: *He **says** he is busy. She **has told** me she can't come.*
2. сообщаемое **всё ещё верно** или относится к будущему и говорится вскоре после слов: > "The meeting starts at six." → She said the meeting **starts** at six. (и это ещё актуально)
3. это **общеизвестный факт**: > The teacher explained that water **boils** at 100°C.
4. прошедшее время и так ясно из контекста: *He said he **went** to Rome last year.* (достаточно past simple вместо past perfect, потому что есть **last year**).
Но если сомневаетесь, сдвиг **всегда допустим**: *She said she lived in Oslo* корректно в любом случае. Не сдвигайте лишь там, где сдвиг дал бы противоречие или неясность.

## Будущее в прошедшем и модальные глаголы
- **will → would**: > "I'll help." → He said he **would** help. **is going to → was going to**.
- **can't → couldn't**, **may** (возможность) → **might**: > "It may rain." → He said it **might** rain.
- **must** (обязанность) → **had to**: > "I must go." → She said she **had to** go. (**must** остаётся, если обязанность актуальна.)
- **shall** (предложение) → **would** / **should**. Также: **has to → had to**, **need to → needed to** (а **needn't** может остаться).

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~She said she will come.~~ (о событии в прошлом) → She said she **would** come.
- ~~He said he has finished.~~ → He said he **had** finished.
- ~~She told me she is tired yesterday.~~ → ...she **was** tired.
- ~~He said he can swim.~~ (в рассказе о прошлом) → he **could** swim.
- ~~They said they would have been late.~~ (о словах "We'll be late") → They said they **would be** late.
en:
## The basic rule: backshift
When the reporting verb is in the past (**said, told, explained, thought**), the verb in the that-clause usually moves one step back in time:
- present simple → **past simple**: > "I work here." → She said she **worked** there.
- present continuous → **past continuous**: > "I'm leaving." → He said he **was leaving**.
- present perfect → **past perfect**: > "We've signed it." → They said they **had signed** it.
- past simple → **past perfect** (or stays past simple): > "I lost the key." → She said she **had lost** the key.
- past continuous → **past perfect continuous** (or stays): > "It was raining." → He said it **had been raining**.
- **will → would**, **can → could**, **may → might**, **shall → should**, **is going to → was going to**, **must → had to**.
The point is to show that the words were spoken in the past.

## What does not change
- **would, could, should, might, ought to, used to, had better, needn't, mustn't**: > "You should rest." → She said I **should** rest.
- **past perfect** stays: *"I had already left."* → *He said he **had** already left.*
- **Hypothetical forms**: > "If I were you, I'd apply." → She said that if she **were** me, she'd apply.
- **must** for deduction: > "She must be tired." → I thought she **must be** tired.

## When backshift is optional
We do not have to shift when:
1. the reporting verb is in the present or present perfect: *He **says** he is busy. She **has told** me she can't come.*
2. what was said is **still true** or still in the future, and we report it soon after: > "The meeting starts at six." → She said the meeting **starts** at six.
3. it is a **general fact**: > The teacher explained that water **boils** at 100°C.
4. the past is clear from the context: *He said he **went** to Rome last year.* (past simple is enough because of **last year**).
If in doubt, backshift is **always possible**: *She said she lived in Oslo* is correct in any case. Do not shift only when it would cause a contradiction or confusion.

## Future in the past and modals
- **will → would**: > "I'll help." → He said he **would** help. **is going to → was going to**.
- **can't → couldn't**, **may** (possibility) → **might**: > "It may rain." → He said it **might** rain.
- **must** (obligation) → **had to**: > "I must go." → She said she **had to** go. (**must** stays if the obligation is still current.)
- **shall** (offer) → **would** / **should**.

## Common mistakes
- ~~She said she will come.~~ (about a past event) → She said she **would** come.
- ~~He said he has finished.~~ → He said he **had** finished.
- ~~She told me she is tired yesterday.~~ → ...she **was** tired.
- ~~He said he can swim.~~ (in a story about the past) → he **could** swim.
structure:
## Сдвиг времён
| Прямая речь | Косвенная речь |
|---|---|
| present simple: *I work* | past simple: *she said she worked* |
| present continuous: *I'm working* | past continuous: *she was working* |
| present perfect: *I've worked* | past perfect: *she had worked* |
| past simple: *I worked* | past perfect (или past simple): *she had worked* |
| past continuous: *I was working* | past perfect continuous (или past continuous) |
| will | would |
| can | could |
| may | might |
| must | had to (must) |
| is / are going to | was / were going to |

## Не меняются
| Форма | Пример |
|---|---|
| would, could, should, might, ought to | He said I **should** rest. |
| past perfect | She said she **had** left. |
| were в условных | He said if he **were** me... |
| must — вывод | I thought she **must be** tired. |

## Правило выбора
> reporting verb в **прошедшем** → сдвиг (всегда допустим)
> reporting verb в **настоящем / present perfect** → без сдвига
> факт **всё ещё верен** → сдвиг не обязателен

exercises.title: Сдвиг времён
exercises.instruction: Примените сдвиг времён (backshift): вводный глагол стоит в прошедшем, слова переданы позже.

items.text: 'I'm working on a new project,' said Lena. → Lena said she {{was working}} on a new project.
'We've finished the report,' they told us. → They told us they {{had finished|'d finished}} the report.
'I'll call you after the meeting,' she said. → She said she {{would call|would phone|'d call|'d phone}} me after the meeting.
'I can't open the file,' said Dan. → Dan said he {{couldn't|could not}} open the file.
'Kate is going to resign,' he said. → He said Kate {{was going to}} resign.
'We drove all night,' they said. → They said they {{had driven|drove}} all night.
'I must leave early,' said Ana. → Ana said she {{had to|must}} leave early.
'It was raining when I left,' he told me. → He told me it {{had been raining|was raining}} when he left.

exercises.title: Что не меняется
exercises.instruction: Впишите слово, которое в косвенной речи остаётся без изменений.

items.text: 'You should rest,' the doctor said. → The doctor said I {{should}} rest.
'I used to live here,' he said. → He said he {{used to}} live there.
'We might be late,' she said. → She said we {{might}} be late.
'She must be exhausted,' I thought. → I thought she {{must|had to}} be exhausted.
'If I were you, I'd apply,' she said. → She said that if she {{were|was}} me, she'd apply.
'We ought to leave,' he said. → He said we {{ought to}} leave.
'You needn't come,' she said. → She said I {{needn't|need not}} come.
'He had already left,' she told me. → She told me he {{had}} already left.

items.q: (Reported after Friday.) 'I'm leaving on Friday,' she said. → She said she ___ on Friday.
(Before his trip to Norway last winter.) 'I have never seen snow,' Tom said. → Tom said he ___ never seen snow.
items.why: present perfect → **past perfect**; **has** не подходит: после поездки это уже неправда.

items.q: (The move was last month.) 'I'll help you with the move,' she said. → She said she ___ help me with the move.
The newspaper says the minister ___ resign tomorrow.
items.why: Вводный глагол в настоящем (**says**) — сдвига нет.

items.q: 'We were waiting for hours,' they complained. → They complained that they ___ for hours.
In the story, 'I can't find the key,' he said. → He said he ___ find the key.
(Reported the next day.) 'I must go now,' said Ann. → Ann said she ___ go.
'He was sleeping when I came,' she said. → She said he ___ when she came.
(Reported years later; the novel came out long ago.) 'I'm working on a novel,' she said. → She said she ___ on a novel.
items.why: Работа над романом давно закончена — сдвиг обязателен: **was working**.

items.q: 'You mustn't open it,' he warned. → He warned me I ___ open it.
'If I were you, I'd apply,' she said. → She said that if she ___ me, she'd apply.
The article says that the company ___ 200 jobs next year.
items.why: Вводный глагол **says** в настоящем — сдвига нет.

items.q: (Reported later.) 'I've been waiting since noon,' he said. → He said he ___ since noon.
items.why: present perfect continuous → past perfect continuous.

items.q: (Reported after six o'clock.) 'I'll be there at six,' she said. → She said she ___ there at six.
'Kate may be late,' he said. → He said Kate ___ be late.
'She must be joking,' I thought. → I thought she ___ joking.

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Ответьте полными предложениями, используя косвенную речь.

items.prompt: Report what someone told you this morning. Use: He/She said (that) ...
items.sample: My colleague said that the meeting had been moved to Friday.

items.prompt: Report a promise somebody made you. Use: said (that) ... would ...
items.sample: My brother said he would visit me in the summer.

items.prompt: Report something you read in the news. Use: the report said (that) ...
items.sample: The report said that prices had risen sharply.

items.prompt: Report what a teacher or boss said about your work.
items.sample: My teacher said I was making good progress.

items.prompt: Report what a friend said about their plans.
items.sample: My friend said she was going to study abroad.
